Hydrogen Bonds
In BIOL 112, we only calling them 
hydrogen bonds if they are PD – PD 
interactions.
Ion– PD interactions are technically still 
hydrogen bonds and this answer here is a 
hold over from previous years when we 
kept that designation.
In 2026/2027 Winter Term 1 we are use 
the PD – PD only definition of hydrogen 
bonds

Learning Outcomes
• Describe how the cell membrane is both a container and semi-
permeable barrier.
• Apply your understanding of chemistry for biology to explain how 
proteins are embedded in or interact with membrane bilayers. To do 
this you will need to be able to:
• Recognize the major ways that proteins are associated with membranes.
• Recognize the types of non-covalent interactions that occur between different 
amino acids, lipids and water.
• Describe the movement of lipids and proteins within the membrane 
according to the fluid mosaic model and recognize why movement 
of membrane components is important for membrane function.

Learning Outcomes
• Using a transport graph for a molecule, predict the type of transport 
occurring (and explain your reasoning in words, clearly connecting your 
explanation to data from a figure). To do this you will need to be able to:
• Recognize that movement of most molecules across membranes is mediated by 
proteins in the membrane.
• Recognize and describe membrane transport proteins (carriers versus channels) and 
list the differences between these types of proteins.
• Recognize and describe between the different types of membrane transport (simple 
diffusion, facilitated diffusion and active transport) in terms of concentration 
dependence, protein transporters, and energy requirements.
• Plot a transport graph comparing the concentration ratios of molecules across 
membranes over time.
• Distinguish between the processes of diffusion and osmosis.
